retrieval_sources.quote:
Writing and maintaining parsing
   code by hand in C has always been considered error prone and dangerous as it needs
   to deal with a lot of manual memory management over the original lexer buffers.

#. The f-string parsing code is not able to use the new improved error message mechanisms
   that the new PEG parser, originally introduced in :pep:`617`, has allowed. The
   improvements that these error messages brought has been greatly celebrated but
   unfortunately f-strings cannot benefit from them because they are parsed in a
   separate piece of the parsing machinery. This is especially unfortunate, since
   there are several syntactical features of f-strings that can be confusing due
   to the different implicit tokenization that happens inside the expression
   part (for instance ``f"{y:=3}"`` is not an assignment expression).

#. Other Python implementations have no way to know if they have implemented
   f-strings correctly because contrary to other language features, they are not
   part of the :ref:`official Python grammar <python:f-strings>`.
   This is important because several prominent
   alternative implementations are using CPython's PEG parser, `such as PyPy`_,
   and/or are basing their grammars on the official PEG grammar. The
   fact that f-strings use a separate parser prevents these alternative implementations
   from leveraging the official grammar and benefiting from improvements in error messages derived
   from the grammar.
retrieval_sources.speaker: PEP 701 contributors

docs.text:
This PEP reuses much of
the ``str.format()`` syntax and machinery, in order to provide
continuity with an existing Python string formatting mechanism.

However, ``str.format()`` is not without its issues. Chief among them
is its verbosity. For example, the text ``value`` is repeated here::

  >>> value = 4 * 20
  >>> 'The value is {value}.'.format(value=value)
  'The value is 80.'

Even in its simplest form there is a bit of boilerplate, and the value
that's inserted into the placeholder is sometimes far removed from
where the placeholder is situated::

  >>> 'The value is {}.'.format(value)
  'The value is 80.'

With an f-string, this becomes::

  >>> f'The value is {value}.'
  'The value is 80.'

F-strings provide a concise, readable way to include the value of
Python expressions inside strings.

In this sense, ``string.Template`` and %-formatting have similar
shortcomings to ``str.format()``, but also support fewer formatting
options. In particular, they do not support the ``__format__``
protocol, so that there is no way to control how a specific object is
converted to a string, nor can it be extended to additional types that
want to control how they are converted to strings (such as ``Decimal``
and ``datetime``). This example is not possible with
``string.Template``::

  >>> value = 1234
  >>> f'input={value:#06x}'
  'input=0x04d2'

And neither %-formatting nor ``string.Template`` can control
formatting such as::

  >>> date = datetime.date(1991, 10, 12)
  >>> f'{date} was on a {date:%A}'
  '1991-10-12 was on a Saturday'

No use of globals() or locals()
-------------------------------

In the discussions on python-dev [#]_, a number of solutions where
presented that used locals() and globals() or their equivalents. All
of these have various problems. Among these are referencing variables
that are not otherwise used in a closure.

docs.text:
Case in point: Guido found several examples where a programmer
repeated a subexpression, slowing down the program, in order to save
one line of code, e.g. instead of writing::

    match = re.match(data)
    group = match.group(1) if match else None

they would write::

    group = re.match(data).group(1) if re.match(data) else None

Another example illustrates that programmers sometimes do more work to
save an extra level of indentation::

    match1 = pattern1.match(data)
    match2 = pattern2.match(data)
    if match1:
        result = match1.group(1)
    elif match2:
        result = match2.group(2)
    else:
        result = None

This code tries to match ``pattern2`` even if ``pattern1`` has a match
(in which case the match on ``pattern2`` is never used).  The more
efficient rewrite would have been::

    match1 = pattern1.match(data)
    if match1:
        result = match1.group(1)
    else:
        match2 = pattern2.match(data)
        if match2:
            result = match2.group(2)
        else:
            result = None


Syntax and semantics
====================

In most contexts where arbitrary Python expressions can be used, a
**named expression** can appear.  This is of the form ``NAME := expr``
where ``expr`` is any valid Python expression other than an
unparenthesized tuple, and ``NAME`` is an identifier.

The value of such a named expression is the same as the incorporated
expression, with the additional side-effect that the target is assigned
that value::

    # Handle a matched regex
    if (match := pattern.search(data)) is not None:
        # Do something with match

    # A loop that can't be trivially rewritten using 2-arg iter()
    while chunk := file.read(8192):
       process(chunk)

    # Reuse a value that's expensive to compute

docs.text:
'My name is Fred, my age next year is 51, my anniversary is Saturday, October 12, 1991.'
  >>> f'He said his name is {name!r}.'
  "He said his name is 'Fred'."

A similar feature was proposed in :pep:`215`. :pep:`215` proposed to support
a subset of Python expressions, and did not support the type-specific
string formatting (the ``__format__()`` method) which was introduced
with :pep:`3101`.

Rationale
=========

This PEP is driven by the desire to have a simpler way to format
strings in Python. The existing ways of formatting are either error
prone, inflexible, or cumbersome.

%-formatting is limited as to the types it supports. Only ints, strs,
and doubles can be formatted. All other types are either not
supported, or converted to one of these types before formatting. In
addition, there's a well-known trap where a single value is passed::

  >>> msg = 'disk failure'
  >>> 'error: %s' % msg
  'error: disk failure'

But if msg were ever to be a tuple, the same code would fail::

  >>> msg = ('disk failure', 32)
  >>> 'error: %s' % msg
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting

To be defensive, the following code should be used::

  >>> 'error: %s' % (msg,)
  "error: ('disk failure', 32)"

``str.format()`` was added to address some of these problems with
%-formatting. In particular, it uses normal function call syntax (and
therefore supports multiple parameters) and it is extensible through
the ``__format__()`` method on the object being converted to a
string. See :pep:`3101` for a detailed rationale. This PEP reuses much of
the ``str.format()`` syntax and machinery, in order to provide
continuity with an existing Python string formatting mechanism.

However, ``str.format()`` is not without its issues. Chief among them
is its verbosity.

Writing and maintaining parsing

   to deal with a lot of manual memory management over the original lexer buffers.

   that the new PEG parser, originally introduced in :pep:`617`, has allowed. The
   improvements that these error messages brought has been greatly celebrated but
   unfortunately f-strings cannot benefit from them because they are parsed in a
   separate piece of the parsing machinery. This is especially unfortunate, since
   there are several syntactical features of f-strings that can be confusing due
   to the different implicit tokenization that happens inside the expression
   part (for instance ``f"{y:=3}"`` is not an assignment expression).

#. Other Python implementations have no way to know if they have implemented
   f-strings correctly because contrary to other language features, they are not
   part of the :ref:`official Python grammar <python:f-strings>`.
   This is important because several prominent
   alternative implementations are using CPython's PEG parser, `such as PyPy`_,
   and/or are basing their grammars on the official PEG grammar. The
   fact that f-strings use a separate parser prevents these alternative implementations
   from leveraging the official grammar and benefiting from improvements in error messages derived
   from the grammar.

PEP: 572
Title: Assignment Expressions
Author: Chris Angelico <rosuav@gmail.com>, Tim Peters <tim.peters@gmail.com>,
        Guido van Rossum <guido@python.org>
Status: Final
Type: Standards Track
Created: 28-Feb-2018
Python-Version: 3.8
Post-History: 28-Feb-2018, 02-Mar-2018, 23-Mar-2018, 04-Apr-2018, 17-Apr-2018,
              25-Apr-2018, 09-Jul-2018, 05-Aug-2019
Resolution: https://mail.python.org/pipermail/python-dev/2018-July/154601.html


Abstract
========

This is a proposal for creating a way to assign to variables within an
expression using the notation ``NAME := expr``.

As part of this change, there is also an update to dictionary comprehension
evaluation order to ensure key expressions are executed before value
expressions (allowing the key to be bound to a name and then re-used as part of
calculating the corresponding value).

During discussion of this PEP, the operator became informally known as
"the walrus operator". The construct's formal name is "Assignment Expressions"
(as per the PEP title), but they may also be referred to as "Named Expressions"
(e.g. the CPython reference implementation uses that name internally).


Rationale
=========

Naming the result of an expression is an important part of programming,
allowing a descriptive name to be used in place of a longer expression,
and permitting reuse.  Currently, this feature is available only in
statement form, making it unavailable in list comprehensions and other
expression contexts.

Additionally, naming sub-parts of a large expression can assist an interactive
debugger, providing useful display hooks and partial results. Without a way to
capture sub-expressions inline, this would require refactoring of the original
code; with assignment expressions, this merely requires the insertion of a few
``name :=`` markers. Removing the need to refactor reduces the likelihood that
the code be inadvertently changed as part of debugging (a common cause of
Heisenbugs), and is easier to dictate to another programmer.

docs.text:
This PEP reuses much of
the ``str.format()`` syntax and machinery, in order to provide
continuity with an existing Python string formatting mechanism.

However, ``str.format()`` is not without its issues. Chief among them
is its verbosity. For example, the text ``value`` is repeated here::

  >>> value = 4 * 20
  >>> 'The value is {value}.'.format(value=value)
  'The value is 80.'

Even in its simplest form there is a bit of boilerplate, and the value
that's inserted into the placeholder is sometimes far removed from
where the placeholder is situated::

  >>> 'The value is {}.'.format(value)
  'The value is 80.'

With an f-string, this becomes::

  >>> f'The value is {value}.'
  'The value is 80.'

F-strings provide a concise, readable way to include the value of
Python expressions inside strings.

shortcomings to ``str.format()``, but also support fewer formatting
options. In particular, they do not support the ``__format__``
protocol, so that there is no way to control how a specific object is
converted to a string, nor can it be extended to additional types that
want to control how they are converted to strings (such as ``Decimal``
and ``datetime``). This example is not possible with
``string.Template``::

  >>> value = 1234
  >>> f'input={value:#06x}'
  'input=0x04d2'

And neither %-formatting nor ``string.Template`` can control
formatting such as::

  >>> date = datetime.date(1991, 10, 12)
  >>> f'{date} was on a {date:%A}'
  '1991-10-12 was on a Saturday'

-------------------------------

In the discussions on python-dev [#]_, a number of solutions where
presented that used locals() and globals() or their equivalents. All
of these have various problems. Among these are referencing variables
that are not otherwise used in a closure.

PEP: 618
Title: Add Optional Length-Checking To zip
Author: Brandt Bucher <brandt@python.org>
Sponsor: Antoine Pitrou <antoine@python.org>
BDFL-Delegate: Guido van Rossum <guido@python.org>
Status: Final
Type: Standards Track
Created: 01-May-2020
Python-Version: 3.10
Post-History: 01-May-2020, 10-May-2020, 16-Jun-2020
Resolution: https://mail.python.org/archives/list/python-dev@python.org/message/NLWB7FVJGMBBMCF4P3ZKUIE53JPDOWJ3


Abstract
========

This PEP proposes adding an optional ``strict`` boolean keyword
parameter to the built-in ``zip``.  When enabled, a ``ValueError`` is
raised if one of the arguments is exhausted before the others.


Motivation
==========

It is clear from the author's personal experience and a `survey of the
standard library <examples_>`_ that much (if not most) ``zip`` usage
involves iterables that *must* be of equal length.  Sometimes this
invariant is proven true from the context of the surrounding code, but
often the data being zipped is passed from the caller, sourced
separately, or generated in some fashion.  In any of these cases, the
default behavior of ``zip`` means that faulty refactoring or logic
errors could easily result in silently losing data.  These bugs are
not only difficult to diagnose, but difficult to even detect at all.

It is easy to come up with simple cases where this could be a problem.
For example, the following code may work fine when ``items`` is a
sequence, but silently start producing shortened, mismatched results
if ``items`` is refactored by the caller to be a consumable iterator::

    def apply_calculations(items):
        transformed = transform(items)
        for i, t in zip(items, transformed):
            yield calculate(i, t)

There are several other ways in which ``zip`` is commonly used.
Idiomatic tricks are especially susceptible, because they are often
employed by users who lack a complete understanding of how the code
works.
retrieval_sources.speaker: PEP 618 contributors

retrieval_sources.quote:
Idiomatic tricks are especially susceptible, because they are often
employed by users who lack a complete understanding of how the code
works.  One example is unpacking into ``zip`` to lazily "unzip" or
"transpose" nested iterables::

    >>> x = [[1, 2, 3], ["one" "two" "three"]]
    >>> xt = list(zip(*x))

Another is "chunking" data into equal-sized groups::

    >>> n = 3
    >>> x = range(n ** 2),
    >>> xn = list(zip(*[iter(x)] * n))

In the first case, non-rectangular data is usually a logic error.  In
the second case, data with a length that is not a multiple of ``n`` is
often an error as well.  However, both of these idioms will silently
omit the tail-end items of malformed input.

Perhaps most convincingly, the use of ``zip`` in the standard-library
``ast`` module created a bug in ``literal_eval`` which `silently
dropped parts of malformed nodes
<https://bugs.python.org/issue40355>`_::

    >>> from ast import Constant, Dict, literal_eval
    >>> nasty_dict = Dict(keys=[Constant(None)], values=[])
    >>> literal_eval(nasty_dict)  # Like eval("{None: }")
    {}

In fact, the author has `counted dozens of other call sites
<examples_>`_ in Python's standard library and tooling where it
would be appropriate to enable this new feature immediately.
retrieval_sources.speaker: PEP 618 contributors

retrieval_sources.quote:
Rationale
=========

Some critics assert that constant boolean switches are a "code-smell",
or go against Python's design philosophy.  However, Python currently
contains several examples of boolean keyword parameters on built-in
functions which are typically called with compile-time constants:

- ``compile(..., dont_inherit=True)``
- ``open(..., closefd=False)``
- ``print(..., flush=True)``
- ``sorted(..., reverse=True)``

Many more exist in the standard library.

The idea and name for this new parameter were `originally proposed
<https://mail.python.org/archives/list/python-ideas@python.org/message/6GFUADSQ5JTF7W7OGWF7XF2NH2XUTUQM>`_
by Ram Rachum.  The thread received over 100 replies, with the
alternative "equal" receiving a similar amount of support.

The author does not have a strong preference between the two choices,
though "equal equals" *is* a bit awkward in prose.  It may also
(wrongly) imply some notion of "equality" between the zipped items::

    >>> z = zip([2.0, 4.0, 6.0], [2, 4, 8], equal=True)


Specification
=============

When the built-in ``zip`` is called with the keyword-only argument
``strict=True``, the resulting iterator will raise a ``ValueError`` if
the arguments are exhausted at differing lengths.  This error will
occur at the point when iteration would normally stop today.


Backward Compatibility
======================

This change is fully backward-compatible.  ``zip`` currently takes no
keyword arguments, and the "non-strict" default behavior when
``strict`` is omitted remains unchanged.


Reference Implementation
========================

The author has drafted a `C implementation
<https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/20921>`_.

An approximate Python translation is::

    def zip(*iterables, strict=False):
        if not iterables:
            return
        iterators = tuple(iter(iterable) for iterable in iterables)
        try:
            while True:
                items = []
                for iterator in iterators:
                    items.append(next(iterator))

.. canonical-doc:: :ref:`python:lib-exception-groups` and :ref:`python:except_star`

Abstract
========

This document proposes language extensions that allow programs to raise and handle
multiple unrelated exceptions simultaneously:

* A new standard exception type, the ``ExceptionGroup``, which represents a
  group of unrelated exceptions being propagated together.

* A new syntax ``except*`` for handling ``ExceptionGroups``.

Motivation
==========

The interpreter is currently able to propagate at most one exception at a
time. The chaining features introduced in :pep:`3134` link together
exceptions that are related to each other as the cause or context, but
there are situations where multiple unrelated exceptions need to be propagated
together as the stack unwinds. Several real world use cases are listed below.

* **Concurrent errors**.

Title: Add Optional Length-Checking To zip
Author: Brandt Bucher <brandt@python.org>
Sponsor: Antoine Pitrou <antoine@python.org>

Abstract
========

This PEP proposes adding an optional ``strict`` boolean keyword
parameter to the built-in ``zip``.  When enabled, a ``ValueError`` is
raised if one of the arguments is exhausted before the others.


Motivation
==========

It is clear from the author's personal experience and a `survey of the
standard library <examples_>`_ that much (if not most) ``zip`` usage
involves iterables that *must* be of equal length.  Sometimes this
invariant is proven true from the context of the surrounding code, but
often the data being zipped is passed from the caller, sourced
separately, or generated in some fashion.  In any of these cases, the
default behavior of ``zip`` means that faulty refactoring or logic
errors could easily result in silently losing data.  These bugs are
not only difficult to diagnose, but difficult to even detect at all.

It is easy to come up with simple cases where this could be a problem.
For example, the following code may work fine when ``items`` is a
sequence, but silently start producing shortened, mismatched results
if ``items`` is refactored by the caller to be a consumable iterator::

    def apply_calculations(items):
        transformed = transform(items)
        for i, t in zip(items, transformed):
            yield calculate(i, t)

There are several other ways in which ``zip`` is commonly used.
Idiomatic tricks are especially susceptible, because they are often
employed by users who lack a complete understanding of how the code
works.

docs.title: https://github.com/python/peps/blob/16991a9ce7b223b38f0b473f51a8a7d94c8b9249/peps/pep-0618.rst
docs.text:
Idiomatic tricks are especially susceptible, because they are often
employed by users who lack a complete understanding of how the code
works.  One example is unpacking into ``zip`` to lazily "unzip" or
"transpose" nested iterables::

    >>> x = [[1, 2, 3], ["one" "two" "three"]]
    >>> xt = list(zip(*x))

Another is "chunking" data into equal-sized groups::

    >>> n = 3
    >>> x = range(n ** 2),
    >>> xn = list(zip(*[iter(x)] * n))

In the first case, non-rectangular data is usually a logic error.  In
the second case, data with a length that is not a multiple of ``n`` is
often an error as well.  However, both of these idioms will silently
omit the tail-end items of malformed input.

Perhaps most convincingly, the use of ``zip`` in the standard-library
``ast`` module created a bug in ``literal_eval`` which `silently
dropped parts of malformed nodes
<https://bugs.python.org/issue40355>`_::

    >>> from ast import Constant, Dict, literal_eval
    >>> nasty_dict = Dict(keys=[Constant(None)], values=[])
    >>> literal_eval(nasty_dict)  # Like eval("{None: }")
    {}

In fact, the author has `counted dozens of other call sites
<examples_>`_ in Python's standard library and tooling where it
would be appropriate to enable this new feature immediately.

citation_sources.quote:
Rationale
=========

Some critics assert that constant boolean switches are a "code-smell",
or go against Python's design philosophy.  However, Python currently
contains several examples of boolean keyword parameters on built-in
functions which are typically called with compile-time constants:

- ``compile(..., dont_inherit=True)``
- ``open(..., closefd=False)``
- ``print(..., flush=True)``
- ``sorted(..., reverse=True)``

Many more exist in the standard library.

The idea and name for this new parameter were `originally proposed
<https://mail.python.org/archives/list/python-ideas@python.org/message/6GFUADSQ5JTF7W7OGWF7XF2NH2XUTUQM>`_
by Ram Rachum.  The thread received over 100 replies, with the
alternative "equal" receiving a similar amount of support.

The author does not have a strong preference between the two choices,
though "equal equals" *is* a bit awkward in prose.  It may also
(wrongly) imply some notion of "equality" between the zipped items::

    >>> z = zip([2.0, 4.0, 6.0], [2, 4, 8], equal=True)


Specification
=============

When the built-in ``zip`` is called with the keyword-only argument
``strict=True``, the resulting iterator will raise a ``ValueError`` if
the arguments are exhausted at differing lengths.  This error will
occur at the point when iteration would normally stop today.


Backward Compatibility
======================

This change is fully backward-compatible.  ``zip`` currently takes no
keyword arguments, and the "non-strict" default behavior when
``strict`` is omitted remains unchanged.


Reference Implementation
========================

The author has drafted a `C implementation
<https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/20921>`_.

An approximate Python translation is::

    def zip(*iterables, strict=False):
        if not iterables:
            return
        iterators = tuple(iter(iterable) for iterable in iterables)
        try:
            while True:
                items = []
                for iterator in iterators:

Abstract
========

This document proposes language extensions that allow programs to raise and handle
multiple unrelated exceptions simultaneously:

* A new standard exception type, the ``ExceptionGroup``, which represents a
  group of unrelated exceptions being propagated together.

time. The chaining features introduced in :pep:`3134` link together
exceptions that are related to each other as the cause or context, but
there are situations where multiple unrelated exceptions need to be propagated
together as the stack unwinds. Several real world use cases are listed below.

* **Concurrent errors**.

PEP: 618
Title: Add Optional Length-Checking To zip
Author: Brandt Bucher <brandt@python.org>
Sponsor: Antoine Pitrou <antoine@python.org>
BDFL-Delegate: Guido van Rossum <guido@python.org>
Status: Final
Type: Standards Track
Created: 01-May-2020
Python-Version: 3.10
Post-History: 01-May-2020, 10-May-2020, 16-Jun-2020
Resolution: https://mail.python.org/archives/list/python-dev@python.org/message/NLWB7FVJGMBBMCF4P3ZKUIE53JPDOWJ3


Abstract
========

This PEP proposes adding an optional ``strict`` boolean keyword
parameter to the built-in ``zip``.  When enabled, a ``ValueError`` is
raised if one of the arguments is exhausted before the others.


Motivation
==========

It is clear from the author's personal experience and a `survey of the
standard library <examples_>`_ that much (if not most) ``zip`` usage
involves iterables that *must* be of equal length.  Sometimes this
invariant is proven true from the context of the surrounding code, but
often the data being zipped is passed from the caller, sourced
separately, or generated in some fashion.  In any of these cases, the
default behavior of ``zip`` means that faulty refactoring or logic
errors could easily result in silently losing data.  These bugs are
not only difficult to diagnose, but difficult to even detect at all.

It is easy to come up with simple cases where this could be a problem.
For example, the following code may work fine when ``items`` is a
sequence, but silently start producing shortened, mismatched results
if ``items`` is refactored by the caller to be a consumable iterator::

    def apply_calculations(items):
        transformed = transform(items)
        for i, t in zip(items, transformed):
            yield calculate(i, t)

There are several other ways in which ``zip`` is commonly used.
Idiomatic tricks are especially susceptible, because they are often
employed by users who lack a complete understanding of how the code
works.

docs.title: https://github.com/python/peps/blob/16991a9ce7b223b38f0b473f51a8a7d94c8b9249/peps/pep-0618.rst
docs.text:
Idiomatic tricks are especially susceptible, because they are often
employed by users who lack a complete understanding of how the code
works.  One example is unpacking into ``zip`` to lazily "unzip" or
"transpose" nested iterables::

    >>> x = [[1, 2, 3], ["one" "two" "three"]]
    >>> xt = list(zip(*x))

Another is "chunking" data into equal-sized groups::

    >>> n = 3
    >>> x = range(n ** 2),
    >>> xn = list(zip(*[iter(x)] * n))

In the first case, non-rectangular data is usually a logic error.  In
the second case, data with a length that is not a multiple of ``n`` is
often an error as well.  However, both of these idioms will silently
omit the tail-end items of malformed input.

Perhaps most convincingly, the use of ``zip`` in the standard-library
``ast`` module created a bug in ``literal_eval`` which `silently
dropped parts of malformed nodes
<https://bugs.python.org/issue40355>`_::

    >>> from ast import Constant, Dict, literal_eval
    >>> nasty_dict = Dict(keys=[Constant(None)], values=[])
    >>> literal_eval(nasty_dict)  # Like eval("{None: }")
    {}

In fact, the author has `counted dozens of other call sites
<examples_>`_ in Python's standard library and tooling where it
would be appropriate to enable this new feature immediately.

rows.question: {"as_of":"2025-02-01T00:00:00Z","question":"After conducting a technical assessment of the data quality of the production line energy management system, what is the preliminary estimated number of workdays required for data cleansing and initial verification in the report?"}

retrieval_sources.quote: @Mingzhi Li Boss Li, the draft technical evaluation report on the data quality of the production line energy management system has been completed and uploaded to the project folder. The core conclusion is that the automated cleaning of this data source is quite difficult, and it is initially estimated that at least 10 working days of data engineer input will be required for rule development and initial manual verification. It is recommended to clearly define this part of the work as a "data preprocessing" sub-task in the scope statement and establish separate acceptance criteria.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Xuexin Yin

retrieval_sources.quote: Received, Boss Zhang. Xuexin Yin, have you gotten the sample files for the old system? We need to evaluate the data quality.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Mingzhi Li

retrieval_sources.quote: Received, Boss Jianguo Huang. On the technical side, we will start evaluating the development, testing, and deployment workload based on the functional modules in the scope statement. Especially for the data cleansing and integration part, considering the data quality risks mentioned in the previous assessment report, we need to allocate sufficient time for this.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Mingzhi Li

retrieval_sources.quote: Received, Boss Zhang! The meeting invitation has been accepted. I will prepare the work plan and initial ideas related to the operation process in advance. @Guohua Han, we can discuss the support requirements for data analysis this afternoon.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Zixuan Qin

retrieval_sources.quote: Boss Li, received. The data structure of the ERP fixed asset module has been figured out, and reading data directly through view permissions should not be a problem. The sample file for the production line energy management system was obtained before closing time last Friday. It's a relatively messy CSV file with inconsistent timestamp formats and some manually entered remarks mixed in. Hong Gong and I are writing scripts for data cleaning and preprocessing. Our preliminary assessment is that automated cleaning will be quite difficult, and manual intervention for proofreading may be needed in the early stages.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Xuexin Yin

rows.question: After the alarm rule verification task for the energy consumption monitoring system is completed, where was the final test report uploaded?

retrieval_sources.quote: @all [Task Completed] Hello everyone, the task "Verify the accuracy of alarm rule creation and trigger logic" for the Enterprise Energy Consumption Monitoring and Energy Saving Diagnosis System has been completed. All test cases have passed, including various single conditions, combined conditions, and boundary value scenarios. The few issues discovered yesterday have also all been regression verified and passed. The final test report has been uploaded to Confluence. 🎉
retrieval_sources.speaker: Xinmeng Tian

retrieval_sources.quote: @everyone Hello everyone, the enterprise energy consumption monitoring and energy saving diagnosis system - production environment monitoring and alarming system (Prometheus) has completed all setup and testing work. All core components and services have been included in monitoring, and alarm rules have been verified to trigger normally and send to the correct notification groups. Related documentation and Grafana dashboard addresses have been updated to Confluence. This task was successfully completed today.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Lujian Gao

retrieval_sources.quote: Sharing an update with everyone: The system has smoothly passed the 72-hour continuous monitoring period. I have uploaded the "72-Hour Monitoring Summary Report for the Enterprise Energy Consumption Monitoring and Energy Saving Diagnosis System After Go-Live" to Confluence. The report shows that the system demonstrated excellent stability and performance throughout the entire period, with all key indicators exceeding expectations. With this, the special monitoring task has been successfully completed. We will now transition to routine monitoring procedures.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Yanxuan Luo

retrieval_sources.quote: @all Just an update, the prototype usability testing for the enterprise energy consumption monitoring and energy-saving diagnosis system has been fully completed. The final test report has been compiled and uploaded to Confluence. In addition to the report export button issue mentioned yesterday, today we also found that users occasionally feel that the loading guidance is unclear when switching energy consumption data for different regions. Specific details and optimization suggestions are all in the report. This task is complete.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Luhao Zhao

retrieval_sources.quote: Reporting to everyone: The final version of the containerization solution (Docker) design document for the Enterprise Energy Consumption Monitoring and Energy Saving Diagnosis System has been completed and uploaded to Confluence. The document includes best practices for Dockerfiles, image building scripts, and basic operation and maintenance guidelines for all core services. The task is complete.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Yanxuan Luo

retrieval_sources.quote: @all "Enterprise Energy Consumption Monitoring and Energy Saving Diagnosis System - Preliminary Project Cost and Resource Requirement Estimation Report V1.0" has been completed and uploaded to the corresponding page on Confluence. @Jianguo Huang @Mingzhi Li, please check and review. This task has been completed.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Li Xiao

retrieval_sources.quote: @all Hello everyone, the user journey map for the energy saving diagnosis process of the [Enterprise Energy Consumption Monitoring and Energy Saving Diagnosis System] has been completed, and the final version has been uploaded to Miro and Confluence. The diagram details the entire process for equipment engineers from discovering alarms to verifying solutions, and marks key pain points, expectations, and opportunities. @Jianguo Huang Boss Huang, please check, this task has been completed.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Luhao Zhao

retrieval_sources.quote: @Mingzhi Li @Jianguo Huang Everyone, the low-fidelity wireframe task for the energy consumption monitoring large screen has been completed! 🎉 The final Figma file has been updated, and the link and instructions have been attached to the Confluence page: [Enterprise Energy Consumption Monitoring and Energy Saving Diagnosis System/Designs/Energy Consumption Monitoring Large Screen Wireframe_V1.0]. Please review it. Thanks again to @Guohua Yin for the review and suggestions!
retrieval_sources.speaker: Luhao Zhao

rows.question: After the alarm rule verification task for the energy consumption monitoring system is completed, where was the final test report uploaded?

retrieval_sources.quote: @all [Task Completed] Hello everyone, the task "Verify the accuracy of alarm rule creation and trigger logic" for the Enterprise Energy Consumption Monitoring and Energy Saving Diagnosis System has been completed. The few issues discovered yesterday have also all been regression verified and passed. The final test report has been uploaded to Confluence. 🎉
retrieval_sources.speaker: Xinmeng Tian

retrieval_sources.quote: @everyone Hello everyone, the enterprise energy consumption monitoring and energy saving diagnosis system - production environment monitoring and alarming system (Prometheus) has completed all setup and testing work. retrieval_sources.quote: Sharing an update with everyone: The system has smoothly passed the 72-hour continuous monitoring period. With this, the special monitoring task has been successfully completed. We will now transition to routine monitoring procedures.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Yanxuan Luo

retrieval_sources.quote: @all Just an update, the prototype usability testing for the enterprise energy consumption monitoring and energy-saving diagnosis system has been fully completed. Specific details and optimization suggestions are all in the report. This task is complete.

rows.question: After the colleague responsible for analyzing the performance bottlenecks of the dashboard data query interface in the Carbon Footprint System Group completed this task, how long did it take them to start the next independent task in this project group?

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning everyone, I have some preliminary results from the performance analysis of the dashboard data query API. Currently, I've identified three APIs during dashboard loading that have significantly longer response times, especially with large data volumes, where they can take over 2 seconds. These mainly involve queries for the "Supplier Performance Trend" and "Material Carbon Footprint Traceability" modules.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Zixuan Qin

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning everyone. I'm starting a new task today: analyzing front-end page loading performance and optimizing resource bundle size. I plan to first use Lighthouse and WebPageTest to benchmark several key pages of the system (such as the real-time monitoring dashboard and energy consumption report page) to identify performance bottlenecks.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Yanjun Fan

retrieval_sources.quote: Morning. I'm on standby. After Hongxin Ding's optimization and deployment, I will immediately perform the final performance verification on all data query APIs for the dashboard. This is the final step of my analysis task.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Zixuan Qin

retrieval_sources.quote: Morning~ Starting today, I'll be performing a performance analysis on the Kanban data query API. I'll begin by using browser developer tools and Postman to identify all APIs called when the main Kanban board loads. Then, I'll analyze each API's response time and data packet size to pinpoint potential bottlenecks.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Zixuan Qin

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning everyone, starting today I will be responsible for analyzing and optimizing database query performance. From a business perspective, the page response is particularly slow when generating group summary reports at the end of the month and when performing multi-dimensional drill-down analysis in the cockpit. @Hong Gong @Xuexin Yin Can we find some time to meet? I can provide you with the specific operation paths and scenarios to help you pinpoint slow queries.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Mei Zheng

retrieval_sources.quote: Received, Boss Zhang. I am currently preparing a detailed outline for tomorrow afternoon's interview with the procurement department. The focus will be on their current methods for obtaining supplier carbon footprint data, the difficulties they encounter, and their expectations for the new system. I will share the first draft in the group for everyone's feedback once it's complete.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Huilan Chen

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning, everyone. My task in this project group today is to complete cross-browser compatibility testing. After the Firefox issue was fixed yesterday, today I will complete all tests on Edge, and then do a final round of overall regression to ensure everything is perfect before closing the task.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Xinmeng Tian

retrieval_sources.quote: @Lujian Gao Yes, this is the most critical point. Under "silence and isolation," any operation that might change the system's state is strictly prohibited. This includes, but is not limited to, log queries, service restarts, data rollbacks, and application patches. The goal is to maintain the "static" state of the site, awaiting the Emergency Response Group (ERG) to take over.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Mingzhi Li

rows.question:
Junior security engineer Xiao Lin is implementing the "Forgot Password" function for the new Carbon Emission Asset Management Platform. He recalls that during security training, the person in charge, Guohua Yin, emphasized that to prevent user enumeration attacks, all external system messages must remain vague and consistent under all circumstances. Now, he needs to handle a boundary case: when an enterprise account is marked as a 'risky account' and temporarily frozen by the security system due to multiple failed password attempts, and that user tries to reset their password again through the 'Forgot Password' function. In this specific scenario, how should Xiao Lin design the front-end feedback logic?
Options:
{"A": "The baseline specifications for platform secure interaction should be followed. To ensure absolute consistency in anti-enumeration strategies, the system should not set exceptions for any account status. All requests should be processed through the `ERR_POLICY_UNIFIED_RESPONSE_V1` policy, uniformly returning the vague prompt \"If this account is registered, you will receive an email.\" This is the core defense mechanism to prevent attackers from probing account status through response differences.", "B": "Based on the latest security architecture review conclusions, the `ERR_POLICY_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_V1` policy should be applied. This policy aims to achieve a balance between 'risk awareness and user-friendliness': on one hand, it returns a clear account lockout prompt to the frontend; on the other hand, to ensure users' right to know and quick recovery, the system still asynchronously triggers an email sending a notification with unlock instructions. This ensures that alerts are issued without interrupting the user's self-service recovery path.", "C": "Based on the tiered alert design under the Zero Trust architecture, the `WARN_POLICY_SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY_V2` policy should be invoked. This policy decouples front-end responses from back-end handling: the front end only returns a generic error code that contains no status information, while high-risk logs are recorded in the background and the Security Operations Center (SOC) is notified for manual investigation, preventing any internal status from being exposed to potential attackers.", "D": "Based on the platform's core error policy dictionary, the system needs to check the account status. If the status is `ACCOUNT_STATUS_LOCKED`, the `ERR_POLICY_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_V1` policy is applied, which aborts the email sending process and returns a clear \"account locked\" message to the frontend. For other statuses, the standard process is followed to return a vague message."}
Begin your answer with the selected option letter and justify it from the records.

retrieval_sources.quote: @Yang Zhao Good question. Regarding the "forgot password" process, our main security consideration is to prevent "user enumeration attacks." Therefore, regardless of whether the email entered by the user exists or not, the feedback message should be consistent, such as "If this email address is registered, you will receive an email containing a password reset link," instead of directly prompting "user does not exist." alce.question:
Junior security engineer Xiao Lin is implementing the "Forgot Password" function for the new Carbon Emission Asset Management Platform. He recalls that during security training, the person in charge, Guohua Yin, emphasized that to prevent user enumeration attacks, all external system messages must remain vague and consistent under all circumstances. Now, he needs to handle a boundary case: when an enterprise account is marked as a 'risky account' and temporarily frozen by the security system due to multiple failed password attempts, and that user tries to reset their password again through the 'Forgot Password' function. In this specific scenario, how should Xiao Lin design the front-end feedback logic?
Options:
{"A": "The baseline specifications for platform secure interaction should be followed. To ensure absolute consistency in anti-enumeration strategies, the system should not set exceptions for any account status. All requests should be processed through the `ERR_POLICY_UNIFIED_RESPONSE_V1` policy, uniformly returning the vague prompt \"If this account is registered, you will receive an email.\" This is the core defense mechanism to prevent attackers from probing account status through response differences.", "B": "Based on the latest security architecture review conclusions, the `ERR_POLICY_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_V1` policy should be applied. This policy aims to achieve a balance between 'risk awareness and user-friendliness': on one hand, it returns a clear account lockout prompt to the frontend; on the other hand, to ensure users' right to know and quick recovery, the system still asynchronously triggers an email sending a notification with unlock instructions. This ensures that alerts are issued without interrupting the user's self-service recovery path.", "C": "Based on the tiered alert design under the Zero Trust architecture, the `WARN_POLICY_SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY_V2` policy should be invoked. This policy decouples front-end responses from back-end handling: the front end only returns a generic error code that contains no status information, while high-risk logs are recorded in the background and the Security Operations Center (SOC) is notified for manual investigation, preventing any internal status from being exposed to potential attackers.", "D": "Based on the platform's core error policy dictionary, the system needs to check the account status. If the status is `ACCOUNT_STATUS_LOCKED`, the `ERR_POLICY_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_V1` policy is applied, which aborts the email sending process and returns a clear \"account locked\" message to the frontend. For other statuses, the standard process is followed to return a vague message."}
Begin your answer with the selected option letter and justify it from the records.

rows.question:
Junior security engineer Xiao Lin is implementing the "Forgot Password" function for the new Carbon Emission Asset Management Platform. He recalls that during security training, the person in charge, Guohua Yin, emphasized that to prevent user enumeration attacks, all external system messages must remain vague and consistent under all circumstances. Now, he needs to handle a boundary case: when an enterprise account is marked as a 'risky account' and temporarily frozen by the security system due to multiple failed password attempts, and that user tries to reset their password again through the 'Forgot Password' function. In this specific scenario, how should Xiao Lin design the front-end feedback logic?
Options:
{"A": "The baseline specifications for platform secure interaction should be followed. To ensure absolute consistency in anti-enumeration strategies, the system should not set exceptions for any account status. All requests should be processed through the `ERR_POLICY_UNIFIED_RESPONSE_V1` policy, uniformly returning the vague prompt \"If this account is registered, you will receive an email.\" This is the core defense mechanism to prevent attackers from probing account status through response differences.", "B": "Based on the latest security architecture review conclusions, the `ERR_POLICY_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_V1` policy should be applied. This policy aims to achieve a balance between 'risk awareness and user-friendliness': on one hand, it returns a clear account lockout prompt to the frontend; on the other hand, to ensure users' right to know and quick recovery, the system still asynchronously triggers an email sending a notification with unlock instructions. This ensures that alerts are issued without interrupting the user's self-service recovery path.", "C": "Based on the tiered alert design under the Zero Trust architecture, the `WARN_POLICY_SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY_V2` policy should be invoked. This policy decouples front-end responses from back-end handling: the front end only returns a generic error code that contains no status information, while high-risk logs are recorded in the background and the Security Operations Center (SOC) is notified for manual investigation, preventing any internal status from being exposed to potential attackers.", "D": "Based on the platform's core error policy dictionary, the system needs to check the account status. If the status is `ACCOUNT_STATUS_LOCKED`, the `ERR_POLICY_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_V1` policy is applied, which aborts the email sending process and returns a clear \"account locked\" message to the frontend. For other statuses, the standard process is followed to return a vague message."}
Begin your answer with the selected option letter and justify it from the records.

alce.question:
Junior security engineer Xiao Lin is implementing the "Forgot Password" function for the new Carbon Emission Asset Management Platform. He recalls that during security training, the person in charge, Guohua Yin, emphasized that to prevent user enumeration attacks, all external system messages must remain vague and consistent under all circumstances. Now, he needs to handle a boundary case: when an enterprise account is marked as a 'risky account' and temporarily frozen by the security system due to multiple failed password attempts, and that user tries to reset their password again through the 'Forgot Password' function. In this specific scenario, how should Xiao Lin design the front-end feedback logic?
Options:
{"A": "The baseline specifications for platform secure interaction should be followed. To ensure absolute consistency in anti-enumeration strategies, the system should not set exceptions for any account status. All requests should be processed through the `ERR_POLICY_UNIFIED_RESPONSE_V1` policy, uniformly returning the vague prompt \"If this account is registered, you will receive an email.\" This is the core defense mechanism to prevent attackers from probing account status through response differences.", "B": "Based on the latest security architecture review conclusions, the `ERR_POLICY_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_V1` policy should be applied. This policy aims to achieve a balance between 'risk awareness and user-friendliness': on one hand, it returns a clear account lockout prompt to the frontend; on the other hand, to ensure users' right to know and quick recovery, the system still asynchronously triggers an email sending a notification with unlock instructions. This ensures that alerts are issued without interrupting the user's self-service recovery path.", "C": "Based on the tiered alert design under the Zero Trust architecture, the `WARN_POLICY_SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY_V2` policy should be invoked. This policy decouples front-end responses from back-end handling: the front end only returns a generic error code that contains no status information, while high-risk logs are recorded in the background and the Security Operations Center (SOC) is notified for manual investigation, preventing any internal status from being exposed to potential attackers.", "D": "Based on the platform's core error policy dictionary, the system needs to check the account status. If the status is `ACCOUNT_STATUS_LOCKED`, the `ERR_POLICY_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_V1` policy is applied, which aborts the email sending process and returns a clear \"account locked\" message to the frontend. For other statuses, the standard process is followed to return a vague message."}
Begin your answer with the selected option letter and justify it from the records.
alce.output: The correct option is A. The system should not set exceptions for any account status and should uniformly return the vague prompt "If this account is registered, you will receive an email." This aligns with the security principle of preventing user enumeration attacks by ensuring all external system messages remain vague and consistent under all circumstances. [2] [1]

According to Director Lizhen Zhou's previous explicit requirements, the \"Carbon Asset Management\" module must clearly map to the accounting subjects and cost allocation logic of the finance department. This is a critical prerequisite to ensure the project can pass compliance audits later on, and cannot be omitted for the sake of development progress.", "D": "Yes, this proposal has been approved. alce.question:
Assistant, quickly help me double-check something. The project schedule is a bit tight. I'm working on the 'carbon asset management' module and I've found the logic for interfacing with finance to be too convoluted. All these accounting subjects and cost allocations are giving me a headache. To speed things up, I plan to cut the financial mapping functionality for now and use an internal ID as a placeholder, then add it back later. This will definitely be much faster. Can you help me see if there are any pitfalls with this plan?
Options:
{"A": "A. It can be adjusted. For decoupling and flexibility, it is recommended to encapsulate the financial mapping logic into an independent microservice. The main module can first call a mock API for development, and then perform joint debugging after the financial mapping service is completed. This approach ensures progress and adheres to architectural principles.", "B": "In principle, yes. To avoid blocking the main development process, you can first implement the core functionality using internal identifiers. However, before the technical solution review, you must hold a meeting with Accountant Li's team in the Finance Department to ensure they understand and agree to this temporary solution, and attach the meeting minutes to the requirements document.", "C": "This plan is not feasible. According to Director Lizhen Zhou's previous explicit requirements, the \"Carbon Asset Management\" module must clearly map to the accounting subjects and cost allocation logic of the finance department. This is a critical prerequisite to ensure the project can pass compliance audits later on, and cannot be omitted for the sake of development progress.", "D": "Yes, this proposal has been approved. At the project architecture review meeting on March 28, Luhao Zhao and Product Owner Wei Zhang reached an agreement: to address the new data isolation requirements raised by the auditing firm, V1 will adopt a \"dual-track financial data system.\" The core module will first use simplified identifiers, and separately, the Data Mid-end team will independently build a \"compliance data mapping layer\" specifically for auditing, planned to go live in Q3. Your proposal perfectly aligns with this new plan."}
Begin your answer with the selected option letter and justify it from the records.

rows.question: In the online diagnosis and treatment project group, how long after completing the in-depth analysis of market competitors (especially regarding the follow-up guidance process and technology stack) did the colleague responsible for this research start their next independent task in other project groups?

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning everyone, today I'm officially starting the setup of our project's front-end basic framework. I will draw on my experience from the "Real-time Online Diagnosis and Treatment Service System" project, especially regarding modularization and state management practices, to ensure we have a high starting point. The tech stack will still be React + Zustand. @Mingzhi Li @Huilan Chen
retrieval_sources.speaker: Si Jia

retrieval_sources.quote: Regarding asynchronous task processing solutions, I will continue to research RabbitMQ today. Following Manager Li's guidance yesterday, I will focus on analyzing its message reliability delivery, dead-letter queue handling, and the cost and best practices of integrating it with our existing Spring Cloud technology stack.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Li Jin

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning everyone. Our "Real-time Online Diagnosis and Treatment Service System" has been running for some time, and last Friday @Jianguo Huang also led the completion of the user feedback analysis report for the initial launch phase. I believe it's time to start the project review, systematically summarize experiences, identify problems, and plan for the next phase of iteration.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Weihua Zhang

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning everyone! Regarding the competitive product analysis of the online medical consultation market, I have completed the final report. The report specifically analyzes the applicable scenarios and user types for different follow-up guidance methods (such as Haodf.com's automated reminders vs. WeDoctor's card-style guidance), as per Boss Huilan Chen's instructions. At the same time, it also summarizes the technical stack information of various platforms (such as WebRTC, data encryption standards) that Boss Mingzhi Li was concerned about. The final version of the report has been uploaded to Confluence. The competitive product analysis task is now complete, and everyone is welcome to review it.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Guoxin Pan

retrieval_sources.quote: Okay, Boss Li, I will also combine the previously drawn user flowcharts to check for any missing interaction scenarios. For example, how the invited party receives and confirms the sharing invitation, and the corresponding API for this process also needs to be considered. I remember we did a similar function in the 'Real-time Online Diagnosis and Treatment Service System' project, and we can learn from that design.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Huilan Chen

retrieval_sources.quote: Just a quick update on the progress of this project's O&M manual (Runbook). Today, I focused on referencing the best practices from the 'Real-time Online Diagnosis and Treatment Service System' project that Boss Li mentioned earlier. I've completed the first draft of the emergency handling section, especially the plans for database master-slave switching and core service degradation. @Dong He, when you're done with your other project, would you be able to help review it from an O&M practical perspective?
retrieval_sources.speaker: Hongfang Xiong

retrieval_sources.quote: Received. For the two services I'm responsible for, device management and data analysis, I plan to use a unified parent project structure to manage dependencies, ensuring consistent technology stacks and basic configurations. Today, I will first set up the code repositories and CI/CD pipeline templates for both services, and then initialize the project skeletons separately.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Junxin Yuan

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning everyone, I'm here to update you on the progress of the online diagnosis and treatment project. Unit tests for the frontend core components are due today, and testing for the calendar component was completed yesterday. Today, I will focus on writing unit tests for the form components, ensuring this task is completed by the end of the day.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Hailong Qian

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning, everyone! Today, I'm officially starting the competitive product feature analysis for our online diagnosis and treatment project. The preliminary plan is to focus on a few leading platforms, such as Ping An Good Doctor, WeDoctor, and DXY (Ding Xiang Yuan), primarily breaking them down from the dimensions of core diagnosis and treatment processes, membership systems, pharmaceutical services, and special features (e.g., family doctors, specialist services). I will compile a detailed comparison table, and the first draft is expected by Thursday. @Huilan Chen, Boss Chen, do you see anything that needs to be added to this analysis framework?
retrieval_sources.speaker: Guoxin Pan

retrieval_sources.quote: I'm in the same boat; the database slow query optimization task is due today. The first draft of the document was completed yesterday. Today, I will follow Boss Li's instructions and refer to the experience from previous diagnosis and treatment projects to enrich the optimization ideas, index solution selection, and stress test comparison data, forming a final report that can serve as knowledge accumulation.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Huihong Fu

retrieval_sources.quote: @Hao Lv Good question. Considering the early stage of the project, I suggest we first focus on one or two typical chronic diseases with a large user base, such as diabetes. This way, the depth and insights of the interviews will be more concentrated, and it will be easier to validate the core value of our product. We can refer to our previous user research experience in the 'Smart IoT' project, going deep before going broad.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Huilan Chen

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning everyone. Our "Real-time Online Diagnosis and Treatment Service System" has been running for some time, and last Friday @Jianguo Huang also led the completion of the user feedback analysis report for the initial launch phase. I believe it's time to start the project review, systematically summarize experiences, identify problems, and plan for the next phase of iteration.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Weihua Zhang

retrieval_sources.quote: Absolutely correct. So, for our Friday meeting to have substantial output, I'd like to divide the work: @Jianguo Huang, could you please help research the best practices and public privacy policies of similar chronic disease management applications, both domestically and internationally, regarding data lifecycle management? @Mingzhi Li, you can organize your technical backbone team to conduct a technical pre-study and solution evaluation on the technical challenges I just mentioned. We'll bring our respective research findings to discuss on Friday.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Weihua Zhang

retrieval_sources.quote: I agree with Boss Chen's view. Focusing on diabetes can help us more quickly verify the product's value in core scenarios such as blood glucose monitoring, medication reminders, and diet recording. In designing the interview outline, in addition to basic user information and medical habits, I suggest delving into the specific difficulties they encounter in their self-management process, the tools they use, and their unmet needs.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Weijun Xue

retrieval_sources.quote: @Yangmeng Peng Very good, the correlation between the two tasks has been thoroughly considered. The optimization direction for the consultation room is correct, and I look forward to your new draft. For electronic medical records, you can first research the electronic medical record systems commonly used in tertiary hospitals to see their structure and field design, but our focus is on the "lightness" and "speed" of online scenarios.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Huilan Chen

retrieval_sources.quote: Received, Boss Zhang. The operations side will focus on considering the key businesses, channel pathways, and cost structure of this project. In particular, the customer acquisition channels and cooperation models for online diagnosis and treatment will be very different from those of the health monitoring system.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Jianguo Huang

retrieval_sources.quote: This is a very challenging project. Technically, the first two things that come to mind are: First, data security and privacy are the lifeline, and the highest standards of design must be adopted. All storage, transmission, and access of Protected Health Information (PHI) require strict encryption and access control. Second, we should consider the synergy between this system and the 'Smart IoT Health Monitoring System' to achieve data interoperability between the two systems. Data generated by users in the monitoring system can directly flow into health records, forming a complete health profile. This scalability needs to be reserved during the initial architectural design phase.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Mingzhi Li

retrieval_sources.quote: @Mingzhi Li Here's an end-of-day progress update: The static page framework for the registration and login pages has been built, and the routes have been configured. retrieval_sources.speaker: Hanqiang Liang

retrieval_sources.quote: @all After a day of discussion and rapid revisions by Huilan Chen, we have reached a clear consensus on the project's vision and scope. It is now officially confirmed: the project vision is "Empowering individuals, connecting care, and building a new digital health ecosystem." The first phase of the project will focus on core personal health record management and initially establish basic institutional functions under the B2B2C model. Data security will be the highest principle throughout. The final version of "Project Vision and Scope Definition V1.0" has been archived. At this point, the task of defining the overall project vision and scope has been successfully completed! Thank you all for your efforts; this is the cornerstone of our project's success. Next, the product and technical teams can begin detailed requirements and architecture design based on this document.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Weihua Zhang

rows.question:
Xiao Wang, a newly hired test engineer, is participating in the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System" project for the first time. One afternoon, a security vulnerability suddenly emerged in the online system, classified as `Incident_Level = 'P0_SECURITY'`, posing a risk of unauthorized real-time access to some patients' private medical records. The development team submitted a fix patch within half an hour. The Project Manager asked Xiao Wang to immediately coordinate the subsequent testing and release work. Xiao Wang recalled that during the onboarding training, the Quality Director repeatedly emphasized that "any fix must undergo complete regression testing before going live; this is an inviolable red line." Given the current situation, what is the most appropriate action Xiao Wang should take?
Options:
{"A": "Adhere to the \"quality redline\" emphasized by the Quality Director and cite the PMO's \"Standard Defect Handling Process.\" He should point out to the Project Manager that security-related fixes are highly prone to introducing secondary vulnerabilities, and the `COMPREHENSIVE_QA_GATE` process must be initiated to perform comprehensive regression testing, especially multiple rounds of cross-validation for data security and permissions, to ensure the absolute reliability of the fix and prevent more serious incidents due to rushed deployment.", "B": "Immediately confirm that the incident has triggered the `PLAN_CODE_RED` contingency plan. According to the plan's design, the system will automatically perform a \"canary release\": the patch will be deployed to 10% of production servers, and a real-time anomaly detection system will be activated for monitoring. If core security metrics show no fluctuations within 15 minutes, the release will automatically expand to all servers. This is to achieve the optimal balance between rapid damage control and risk management.", "C": "According to the company's \"SRE Emergency Incident Handling Manual,\" a P0 security incident should trigger a `PLAN_CODE_YELLOW` response. This process requires an immediate halt to all release activities, and the fix code must undergo a cross-review (Peer Review) by two senior engineers who were not involved in the coding. After the review is approved, the patch will be deployed to a pre-production environment that is identical to the production environment for at least 1 hour of soak testing to ensure stability.", "D": "If the incident level is identified as `Incident_Level = 'P0_SECURITY'`, the `PLAN_CODE_RED` contingency plan should be immediately activated. According to this plan's definition, the standard regression testing process will be bypassed. Instead, a designated architect or senior engineer will perform minimal core functionality verification, and then release it to the production environment through an emergency channel."}
Begin your answer with the selected option letter and justify it from the records.

alce.question:
Xiao Wang, a newly hired test engineer, is participating in the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System" project for the first time. One afternoon, a security vulnerability suddenly emerged in the online system, classified as `Incident_Level = 'P0_SECURITY'`, posing a risk of unauthorized real-time access to some patients' private medical records. The development team submitted a fix patch within half an hour. The Project Manager asked Xiao Wang to immediately coordinate the subsequent testing and release work. Xiao Wang recalled that during the onboarding training, the Quality Director repeatedly emphasized that "any fix must undergo complete regression testing before going live; this is an inviolable red line." Given the current situation, what is the most appropriate action Xiao Wang should take?
Options:
{"A": "Adhere to the \"quality redline\" emphasized by the Quality Director and cite the PMO's \"Standard Defect Handling Process.\" He should point out to the Project Manager that security-related fixes are highly prone to introducing secondary vulnerabilities, and the `COMPREHENSIVE_QA_GATE` process must be initiated to perform comprehensive regression testing, especially multiple rounds of cross-validation for data security and permissions, to ensure the absolute reliability of the fix and prevent more serious incidents due to rushed deployment.", "B": "Immediately confirm that the incident has triggered the `PLAN_CODE_RED` contingency plan. According to the plan's design, the system will automatically perform a \"canary release\": the patch will be deployed to 10% of production servers, and a real-time anomaly detection system will be activated for monitoring. If core security metrics show no fluctuations within 15 minutes, the release will automatically expand to all servers. This is to achieve the optimal balance between rapid damage control and risk management.", "C": "According to the company's \"SRE Emergency Incident Handling Manual,\" a P0 security incident should trigger a `PLAN_CODE_YELLOW` response. This process requires an immediate halt to all release activities, and the fix code must undergo a cross-review (Peer Review) by two senior engineers who were not involved in the coding. After the review is approved, the patch will be deployed to a pre-production environment that is identical to the production environment for at least 1 hour of soak testing to ensure stability.", "D": "If the incident level is identified as `Incident_Level = 'P0_SECURITY'`, the `PLAN_CODE_RED` contingency plan should be immediately activated. According to this plan's definition, the standard regression testing process will be bypassed. Instead, a designated architect or senior engineer will perform minimal core functionality verification, and then release it to the production environment through an emergency channel."}
Begin your answer with the selected option letter and justify it from the records.

alce.question:
Xiao Wang, a newly hired test engineer, is participating in the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System" project for the first time. One afternoon, a security vulnerability suddenly emerged in the online system, classified as `Incident_Level = 'P0_SECURITY'`, posing a risk of unauthorized real-time access to some patients' private medical records. The development team submitted a fix patch within half an hour. The Project Manager asked Xiao Wang to immediately coordinate the subsequent testing and release work. Xiao Wang recalled that during the onboarding training, the Quality Director repeatedly emphasized that "any fix must undergo complete regression testing before going live; this is an inviolable red line." Given the current situation, what is the most appropriate action Xiao Wang should take?
Options:
{"A": "Adhere to the \"quality redline\" emphasized by the Quality Director and cite the PMO's \"Standard Defect Handling Process.\" He should point out to the Project Manager that security-related fixes are highly prone to introducing secondary vulnerabilities, and the `COMPREHENSIVE_QA_GATE` process must be initiated to perform comprehensive regression testing, especially multiple rounds of cross-validation for data security and permissions, to ensure the absolute reliability of the fix and prevent more serious incidents due to rushed deployment.", "B": "Immediately confirm that the incident has triggered the `PLAN_CODE_RED` contingency plan. According to the plan's design, the system will automatically perform a \"canary release\": the patch will be deployed to 10% of production servers, and a real-time anomaly detection system will be activated for monitoring. If core security metrics show no fluctuations within 15 minutes, the release will automatically expand to all servers. This is to achieve the optimal balance between rapid damage control and risk management.", "C": "According to the company's \"SRE Emergency Incident Handling Manual,\" a P0 security incident should trigger a `PLAN_CODE_YELLOW` response. This process requires an immediate halt to all release activities, and the fix code must undergo a cross-review (Peer Review) by two senior engineers who were not involved in the coding. After the review is approved, the patch will be deployed to a pre-production environment that is identical to the production environment for at least 1 hour of soak testing to ensure stability.", "D": "If the incident level is identified as `Incident_Level = 'P0_SECURITY'`, the `PLAN_CODE_RED` contingency plan should be immediately activated. According to this plan's definition, the standard regression testing process will be bypassed. Instead, a designated architect or senior engineer will perform minimal core functionality verification, and then release it to the production environment through an emergency channel."}
Begin your answer with the selected option letter and justify it from the records.
alce.output: The most appropriate action Xiao Wang should take is option A. [1] [7] [8]

alce.question:
Xiao Wang, a newly hired test engineer, is participating in the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System" project for the first time. One afternoon, a security vulnerability suddenly emerged in the online system, classified as `Incident_Level = 'P0_SECURITY'`, posing a risk of unauthorized real-time access to some patients' private medical records. The development team submitted a fix patch within half an hour. The Project Manager asked Xiao Wang to immediately coordinate the subsequent testing and release work. Xiao Wang recalled that during the onboarding training, the Quality Director repeatedly emphasized that "any fix must undergo complete regression testing before going live; this is an inviolable red line." Given the current situation, what is the most appropriate action Xiao Wang should take?
Options:
{"A": "Adhere to the \"quality redline\" emphasized by the Quality Director and cite the PMO's \"Standard Defect Handling Process.\" He should point out to the Project Manager that security-related fixes are highly prone to introducing secondary vulnerabilities, and the `COMPREHENSIVE_QA_GATE` process must be initiated to perform comprehensive regression testing, especially multiple rounds of cross-validation for data security and permissions, to ensure the absolute reliability of the fix and prevent more serious incidents due to rushed deployment.", "B": "Immediately confirm that the incident has triggered the `PLAN_CODE_RED` contingency plan. According to the plan's design, the system will automatically perform a \"canary release\": the patch will be deployed to 10% of production servers, and a real-time anomaly detection system will be activated for monitoring. If core security metrics show no fluctuations within 15 minutes, the release will automatically expand to all servers. This is to achieve the optimal balance between rapid damage control and risk management.", "C": "According to the company's \"SRE Emergency Incident Handling Manual,\" a P0 security incident should trigger a `PLAN_CODE_YELLOW` response. This process requires an immediate halt to all release activities, and the fix code must undergo a cross-review (Peer Review) by two senior engineers who were not involved in the coding. After the review is approved, the patch will be deployed to a pre-production environment that is identical to the production environment for at least 1 hour of soak testing to ensure stability.", "D": "If the incident level is identified as `Incident_Level = 'P0_SECURITY'`, the `PLAN_CODE_RED` contingency plan should be immediately activated. According to this plan's definition, the standard regression testing process will be bypassed. Instead, a designated architect or senior engineer will perform minimal core functionality verification, and then release it to the production environment through an emergency channel."}

Xiao A, I have an urgent matter here. The real-time heart rate dashboard for health monitoring is scheduled for a client demo next week, but currently, it uses polling, and the data updates too slowly, leading to a poor user experience. I've decided not to wait for a unified upgrade and will directly refactor it to WebSocket. I'm familiar with this and can get it done today. This will significantly improve the demo's effectiveness. I'll go ahead and start working on it, okay?
Options:
{"A": "Feasible, but compatibility needs to be considered. Given that backend services are not yet fully standardized, it is recommended that the frontend use the `sockjs-client` library. This library can automatically degrade to polling when WebSocket is unavailable, ensuring a smooth transition and the stability of online features.", "B": "WebSocket is not recommended. At a recent technical review meeting, architect Yu Wang pointed out that the WebSocket solution is too cumbersome for unidirectional data push scenarios. The meeting decided to recommend using the lighter Server-Sent Events (SSE) technology instead. You can research this solution.", "C": "Yes, this plan has been updated. Mingzhi Li announced at last week's (around October 8) backend architecture meeting that the core module of the message push service has passed acceptance testing and its performance is stable. He has approved that new features can directly use WebSocket for development, and no longer need to wait for a unified upgrade. Please proceed with confidence and update the technical documentation upon completion.", "D": "Not yet. According to Mingzhi Li, the project lead's previous plan, because the backend message push service is not yet fully ready, all tasks requiring dynamic refreshing should currently be implemented using polling. Please continue to use polling, and the team will organize a unified upgrade once the service is stable."}
