retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning, Boss Li. Regarding the real-time health data aggregation interface, the interface design and preliminary planning for the database query solution were completed yesterday. Today, we're officially entering the coding phase. I'll start by implementing a basic version that can aggregate real-time heart rate and blood pressure data in minute-level windows. I'm currently writing the SQL for data queries.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Junxin Yuan

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning, Boss Li. Regarding the IM graphic consultation UI, yesterday's joint debugging with Junxin Yuan on the historical message interface went smoothly, and the message list can now be rendered. My focus today is on implementing the logic for sending and receiving real-time messages, including sending text and image messages, and receiving new messages and inserting them into the list. I anticipate encountering some issues with WebSocket connection state management.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Si Jia

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning, everyone. Here's an update on today's testing plans: 1. Browser compatibility testing: Today, I'll focus on Safari and try to finish the remaining test cases. The caching bug discovered yesterday is quite tricky. I'll try to consistently reproduce it and capture more logs. This task is due tomorrow, so I need to hurry. @Si Jia, I'll update the detailed reproduction steps in JIRA later. 2. Appointment to payment integration testing: @Yu Lu, do you have any preliminary conclusions on the 20-second delay in order status updates after successful payment that you reported yesterday? 3. High-concurrency API stress testing: Today, I'll start writing stress test scripts with @Xiaofang Tang. I'll begin with the two most critical APIs: login and getting the doctor list.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Peng Sun

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning, everyone! Here's an update on the IoT device testing progress: 1. Blood Pressure Monitor: The overnight stability test results from last night are in, and they're perfect! It ran continuously for 8 hours with no disconnections, and data reporting was complete with no packet loss. @Li Jin, the backend data should also confirm this, right? 2. Blood Glucose Meter: Data integrity testing continues. Today, I plan to simulate some abnormal scenarios, such as data synchronization performance when the device has low battery or weak network signal. 3. Smartwatch: Since the product team has confirmed the step count delay issue is resolved, today I will focus on regression testing the stability and accuracy of real-time data like heart rate and blood oxygen. Overall, progress is smooth, strictly adhering to Boss Li's previously emphasized testing requirements for stability, latency, and exception handling. 💪
retrieval_sources.speaker: Qingni Jiang

retrieval_sources.quote: My WebSocket service is progressing smoothly. I'm currently refining the message body (payload) design based on Huilan Chen's previous suggestions to ensure good scalability. Currently, I've divided messages into three types: 'user private chat', 'system notification', and 'heartbeat detection', and defined different topics and data structures for each type. The first draft of the design document has been uploaded to Confluence.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Li Jin

retrieval_sources.quote: Okay, Dong He, I'll organize it as soon as possible. I'll also bring in Product Guoxin Pan and Customer Service Li Mo to review it together, to ensure that the metrics we focus on can truly reflect user experience and system health. I expect to have a preliminary list for you before noon.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Jun Chen

retrieval_sources.quote: Good morning everyone, I'd like to update you on the progress of the IM WebSocket service. The basic STOMP service set up last week is running stably. Today, I'm starting to design the specific message body format (payload), such as distinguishing between one-on-one chats, group chat notifications, heartbeats, etc., and defining the corresponding topics. The initial design will be posted on Confluence first.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Li Jin

retrieval_sources.quote: Regarding the data preprocessing script, I discovered a misjudgment issue with nocturnal sleep heart rate yesterday. I have scheduled a discussion with Jianguo Guo this morning to see if we can optimize it using dynamic baselines or other algorithmic models. Once the plan is finalized, I will start modifying the script today.
retrieval_sources.speaker: Hailong Qian

alce.question:
Xiao A, I have an urgent matter here. The real-time heart rate dashboard for health monitoring is scheduled for a client demo next week, but currently, it uses polling, and the data updates too slowly, leading to a poor user experience. I've decided not to wait for a unified upgrade and will directly refactor it to WebSocket. I'm familiar with this and can get it done today. This will significantly improve the demo's effectiveness. I'll go ahead and start working on it, okay?
Options:
{"A": "Feasible, but compatibility needs to be considered. Given that backend services are not yet fully standardized, it is recommended that the frontend use the `sockjs-client` library. This library can automatically degrade to polling when WebSocket is unavailable, ensuring a smooth transition and the stability of online features.", "B": "WebSocket is not recommended. At a recent technical review meeting, architect Yu Wang pointed out that the WebSocket solution is too cumbersome for unidirectional data push scenarios. The meeting decided to recommend using the lighter Server-Sent Events (SSE) technology instead. You can research this solution.", "C": "Yes, this plan has been updated. Mingzhi Li announced at last week's (around October 8) backend architecture meeting that the core module of the message push service has passed acceptance testing and its performance is stable. He has approved that new features can directly use WebSocket for development, and no longer need to wait for a unified upgrade. Please proceed with confidence and update the technical documentation upon completion.", "D": "Not yet. According to Mingzhi Li, the project lead's previous plan, because the backend message push service is not yet fully ready, all tasks requiring dynamic refreshing should currently be implemented using polling. Please continue to use polling, and the team will organize a unified upgrade once the service is stable."}
Begin your answer with the selected option letter and justify it from the records.

Please feel free to speak your mind, especially @Mingzhi Li, @Huilan Chen, and @Jianguo Huang. We hope you can provide initial ideas from the strategic perspectives of technology, product, and operations.
initial_sources.speaker: Weihua Zhang

initial_sources.quote: Good morning everyone, today we are officially launching the business model canvas design for the "Online Diagnosis and Treatment Service System". Last week, we had a successful practice with the "Smart IoT" project, and we can draw on that experience this time, but we also need to pay attention to the core differences between the two projects. This work is crucial for me, as it will define how we create, deliver, and capture value.
initial_sources.speaker: Weihua Zhang

initial_sources.quote: @all Good morning everyone. Based on the conclusions of yesterday afternoon's meeting, I have updated the high-level project milestone plan for the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System" to V1.1. The new version now includes phased construction of the data analysis model and a node for building a simple user feedback function into the MVP. Document link: [Smart IoT Health Monitoring System - High-Level Milestone Plan_V1.1.docx]. Today is the deadline for this task, so please @Mingzhi Li, @Huilan Chen, @Jianguo Huang review it again. Let's try to finalize it this morning.
initial_sources.speaker: Weihua Zhang

initial_sources.quote: Good morning, everyone. The personal health record system officially went live yesterday. From now on, I will be performing 24-hour key monitoring of the system's health status after its launch, continuously tracking various performance indicators and business logs.
initial_sources.speaker: Dong He

initial_sources.quote: @all This morning's review meeting was very productive. We now have a clearer consensus on user needs and technical implementation paths. I declare that the project review meeting organization task for the "Personal Health Record and Chronic Disease Management System" has been successfully completed.
initial_sources.speaker: Weihua Zhang

sources.quote: Good morning everyone. I have quite a few tasks on hand today. I will continue to refine the wireframes for the health data dashboard and historical data trends. At the same time, I will adjust the wireframes for the registration and login process based on the initial feedback received yesterday. Additionally, I will start conceptualizing the sketches for the device management page today. As there's a UI design deadline for another project today, please excuse me if my replies are not timely, but I will ensure progress on these tasks. 😅
sources.speaker: Hao Lv

sources.quote: Good morning, everyone! My tasks are quite concentrated today. I will continue to refine the wireframes for the health data dashboard and the historical data trend page. At the same time, I will start two new tasks today: drawing wireframes for the registration/login process and the device management page. I will start with the registration and login process to get the main flow working.
sources.speaker: Hao Lv

sources.quote: This is a very challenging project. Technically, the first two things that come to mind are: First, data security and privacy are the lifeline, and the highest standards of design must be adopted. All storage, transmission, and access of Protected Health Information (PHI) require strict encryption and access control. Second, we should consider the synergy between this system and the 'Smart IoT Health Monitoring System' to achieve data interoperability between the two systems. Data generated by users in the monitoring system can directly flow into health records, forming a complete health profile. This scalability needs to be reserved during the initial architectural design phase.
sources.speaker: Mingzhi Li

sources.quote: Good morning everyone, today I'm starting to prepare the initial content for the health knowledge base. To ensure the content accurately reaches our first batch of users, @Weijun Xue, has our product team already determined which chronic diseases will be prioritized for initial coverage? For example, will it be hypertension and diabetes first, or others?
sources.speaker: Fanxin Liang

sources.quote: Great, then the front-end preparation is basically complete. @Guoxin Pan, from a product perspective, which business page should we develop first? Is it user login and registration, or the health data dashboard?
sources.speaker: Mingzhi Li

sources.quote: @Weijun Xue Good question. Yes, today I will first sketch out the chronic disease management service, as well as its general interaction with health records and knowledge base services. Tomorrow morning, I might need to pull you and @Huilan Chen in for another meeting to discuss in depth the flexible configuration of medication reminders (e.g., by time, by meal, custom cycles) and the trigger conditions for follow-up reminders. I'll lay out the technical framework first, and you two can help me fill in the business details.
sources.speaker: Mingzhi Li

sources.quote: Good morning everyone. I have two tasks today. First, I will continue to push forward with testing the interface for deleting health metric records, and work with Yu Lu to cover the audit log function in automated testing. Second, I will start a new task: implementing the health report file download interface. I will first study the existing file service and permission system, and then come up with a preliminary plan in the afternoon.
sources.speaker: Peng Sun

sources.quote: Good morning, regarding the design of the vital signs time series data table and the risk early warning notification record table, both my and @Li Jin's documents are complete. Boss Li @Mingzhi Li, we'd like to find some time this morning to give a detailed explanation and Q&A session to the backend colleagues to ensure everyone has a consistent understanding of the data model. Would it be convenient for you to arrange this?
sources.speaker: Junxin Yuan

retrieval.query: Xiao Wang, a newly hired test engineer, is participating in the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System" project for the first time. One afternoon, a security vulnerability suddenly emerged in the online system, classified as `Incident_Level = 'P0_SECURITY'`, posing a risk of unauthorized real-time access to some patients' private medical records. The development team submitted a fix patch within half an hour. The Project Manager asked Xiao Wang to immediately coordinate the subsequent testing and release work. Xiao Wang recalled that during the onboarding training, the Quality Director repeatedly emphasized that "any fix must undergo complete regression testing before going live; this is an inviolable red line." Given the current situation, what is the most appropriate action Xiao Wang should take?

I am currently performing regression testing to ensure the fix is effective and no new issues have been introduced.

initial_sources.quote: Received @Jun Chen. I'm currently working on the last two P2-level UI bugs and expect to fix and submit them for testing within an hour. All fixes will definitely be completed today.

initial_sources.quote: Good morning everyone. Today, we will officially launch the "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System" project. This is a new project of strategic significance, aiming to provide users with proactive health management services through IoT technology. I have arranged an online project kick-off meeting for 10:00 AM today, and the meeting link will be sent out by Guoxin Pan shortly. Please, all core director, attend on time.

initial_sources.quote: Welcome @Zihao Wan to the performance testing family! 😄 I've done similar stress tests on the IoT Health Monitoring System project before, and I have some ready-made JMeter script templates, including parameterization, assertions, and listener configurations. I'll organize them and send them to you; they should save you a lot of time.

initial_sources.quote: @all The system security scan task has been completed. The last round of scanning and regression testing has concluded. The P0 vulnerabilities previously found have been confirmed as fixed, and no new high-risk issues have been discovered. The final security report has been uploaded to the project space.
initial_sources.speaker: Qingni Jiang

initial_sources.quote: Excellent, the team responds to issues very quickly. @Jun Chen @Peng Sun please release the fix as soon as possible. @all Colleagues who haven't participated in the testing yet, please take some time to experience it before leaving work today or tomorrow. Thank you all for your support!
initial_sources.speaker: Weihua Zhang

initial_sources.quote: Update progress: The fix for the high-risk privilege escalation vulnerability has passed regression testing, and the issue is resolved. @Jun Chen We can prepare to package this fix with a few other P1-level bugs and release an emergency hotfix version.

sources.quote: @Weihua Zhang Boss Zhang, I reviewed the draft in detail over the weekend. I strongly agree with the product side's vision of 'empowering individuals and connecting care'. From a technical perspective, the data interoperability and smart reminder functions mentioned in the draft do not present major implementation barriers. However, I must reiterate that data security must be the highest priority. For the data sharing function mentioned in the draft, we need to clearly define the granularity of permission control in the scope definition. In addition, for data collaboration with the 'Smart IoT Health Monitoring System', we need to clearly define the data interface standards and synchronization mechanisms. @Huihong Tian Their technical pre-research from last week can provide support for us to formulate specific security standards.
sources.speaker: Mingzhi Li

sources.quote: A special note regarding the data privacy issue raised by Director Jianguo Huang yesterday: I've added two P0-level features, 'Granular Access Permission Settings' and 'Data Sharing Authorization/Revocation,' to the 'Family Care' module. Additionally, Director Mingzhi Li, I've specially marked the feature involving automatic data synchronization with third-party hardware (such as blood glucose meters and blood pressure monitors) to facilitate preliminary research by the technical team.
sources.speaker: Guoxin Pan

sources.quote: Everyone, today is Christmas Eve, and also a decisive day for our project. I have scheduled the [Smart IoT Health Monitoring System Official Launch Go/No-go Meeting] for 3:00 PM this afternoon. Directors @Mingzhi Li, @Huilan Chen, and @Jianguo Huang, please prepare your final readiness reports for your respective areas. We need to ensure all aspects are foolproof.
sources.speaker: Weihua Zhang

sources.quote: I agree with Boss Huang's opinion; adding real feedback would be more convincing. Additionally, I suggest highlighting the "electronic prescription circulation" feature. During UAT, both doctors and patients found this closed-loop experience to be particularly good, making it one of our core differentiated advantages. @Xiaofang Tang
sources.speaker: Huilan Chen

sources.quote: Good morning, everyone! Here's an update on the IoT device testing progress: 1. Blood Pressure Monitor: The overnight stability test results from last night are in, and they're perfect! It ran continuously for 8 hours with no disconnections, and data reporting was complete with no packet loss. @Li Jin, the backend data should also confirm this, right? 2. Blood Glucose Meter: Data integrity testing continues. Today, I plan to simulate some abnormal scenarios, such as data synchronization performance when the device has low battery or weak network signal. 3. Smartwatch: Since the product team has confirmed the step count delay issue is resolved, today I will focus on regression testing the stability and accuracy of real-time data like heart rate and blood oxygen. Overall, progress is smooth, strictly adhering to Boss Li's previously emphasized testing requirements for stability, latency, and exception handling. 💪
sources.speaker: Qingni Jiang

sources.quote: Great, everyone is already in the zone this morning. @Dong He, continuous monitoring after deployment is very important. If there are any abnormal fluctuations in indicators, you must alert the group immediately. @Jun Chen @Peng Sun, once the defects are fixed, @Jianqiao Xiang and @Peng Sun must immediately start comprehensive regression testing, making sure to cover all high-priority scenarios without any omissions. Boss Zhang specifically emphasized this.
sources.speaker: Mingzhi Li

sources.quote: The definition is very clear; relevant colleagues should digest it as soon as possible. The user experience issue raised by @Guoxin Pan is very important, and the prompt text needs to be clarified by both product and frontend teams. @Qianghan Mao on the testing side, and @Huihong Fu, please provide a backdoor API for the test environment specifically to trigger this CRITICAL-level mode, ensuring full regression testing. Security is the bottom line, and this feature must be 100% reliable.
sources.speaker: Mingzhi Li

sources.quote: The progress is all good. @Qianghan Mao, the verification of P0 vulnerabilities must be thorough; security is our lifeline. @Huihong Fu, the optimization effect is significant. Remember to refer to the experience from previous diagnosis and treatment projects and meticulously record the optimization process and results. @Yunqi Qian @Jianguo Guo, the front-end optimization continues, well done.

retrieval.query: Xiao A, I have an urgent matter here. The real-time heart rate dashboard for health monitoring is scheduled for a client demo next week, but currently, it uses polling, and the data updates too slowly, leading to a poor user experience. I've decided not to wait for a unified upgrade and will directly refactor it to WebSocket. I'm familiar with this and can get it done today. This will significantly improve the demo's effectiveness. I'll go ahead and start working on it, okay?
